title: feat(plugin-auth): a page navigation to the mobile hand-off that has to sign in first goes to the sign-in page
body:
domain:server#2 · hotlong · session_c967d7a472b0485c94711bfcb22159c8

Fixes #29997

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：手机 App 登录现在只需打开交接接口这一个地址。没登录、或会话超过 5 分钟的用户在系统浏览器里打开它，服务端直接跳到本部署的 Console 登录页，登录后回到交接接口，再把一次性令牌交回 App。App 自己的探测请求仍然拿到 401。登录页也一起改了：服务端跳转时写明拒绝时间，登录页按这个时间判断会话，不再只看设备时钟。
- **为什么改**：Google 这类不允许内嵌 WebView 的登录方式走这条流程，装好的 App 会用好几个月。原来 App 要自己知道 Console 登录页的路径和它怎么处理 `redirect`，Console 一升级改了其中一个，这些用户就卡在没有退路的页面上，App 也察觉不到。
- **风险与回滚**：目前还没有已发布的 App 在用这条流程，所以不存在受影响的旧版；现有入口（直接打开 Console 登录页）对用它的构建照常可用。这是会话转移流程，但没有新增能力：令牌仍只发给 5 分钟内登录的会话，跨站打开和非法参数仍先回 400，不会跳到登录页；没挂 Console 的部署保持 401。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.ts` 里的 `refusedSessionAnswer`（什么时候跳、什么时候还回 401）和 `resolveHandoffSignInEntry`（只取路径不换源、怎么判断有没有 Console）；`ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/handoffRedirect.ts` 里的 `isHandoffSessionFresh`（登录页何时放行）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth^...' build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/one-time-token-handoff.test.ts`，预期 88 条全部通过；`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/handoffRedirect-29971.test.ts apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/signInHandoff-29971.test.tsx`，预期 68 条全部通过。
- **需要你做的**：这是会话转移（auth）流程，请维护者审阅并合并本 PR。

## What changes

`GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff`, for a valid request whose session is missing or older than five minutes:

| Request | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| A page navigation | `302` to this deployment's Console sign-in page, with `redirect` naming the same request and `handoff_refused_at` carrying the server's time of the refusal |
| Anything else (the app's probe included) | `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, as before |
| A page navigation reporting `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, which is the sign-in page forwarding | `401`, never another redirect |
| A page navigation when this process does not answer the sign-in page with `200 text/html`, or when the path would start with `//` | `401`, logged once at `warn` |

Nothing else on the route moves. `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is still judged first, then the closed query set, the registered scheme and the challenge; an invalid request gets `400` and never reaches the sign-in page. A token is still minted only for a session under five minutes old (ruling A on #29714).

The Console's sign-in page (`handoffRedirect.ts`): when the query has `handoff_refused_at`, a session with a `createdAt` is fresh only if it was created after that time. The device's clock is not read for it. A value that is not a whole number of milliseconds is ignored, and a session with no `createdAt` keeps its existing branch. The links between `/login` and `/register` carry the mark beside a hand-off `redirect`, and every other link is byte-identical.

Spec: docblock only. Route ledger: the note. No schema, export or generated artefact moved.

## Design

**Telling a page navigation from an API call (constraint 1).** `Sec-Fetch-Dest` decides when a browser sends it: `document` is a navigation, and `empty` (a `fetch`) or `iframe` is not, whatever `Accept` says. With no Fetch Metadata, `Accept` naming `text/html` counts. A request with neither gets the `401`, which is what this route answered before. So the rule rests on no single header, and if a real system auth session turned out to send neither, the result is today's JSON rather than a wrong redirect.

NOT MEASURED: the headers a real `ASWebAuthenticationSession` or Custom Tabs sends. I cannot measure those here. Measured in headless Chromium 151 opening the route directly: `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`, `Sec-Fetch-Site: none`, `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, an HTML `Accept`. The WebKit and Firefox builds Playwright has on this machine do not match its version, so they were not read either.

**Staying on the origin (constraint 3).** `AuthManager.getConsoleUrl` composes `${canonical origin}${uiBasePath}${path}` (confirmed in source), so using it as `Location` would move a browser that reached the deployment on another host. `Location` is root-relative and takes only the path of that URL, which keeps `uiBasePath` and any base path in `baseUrl` honoured without a second composer. Measured through a proxy on another port: the browser stayed on the proxy's origin through the sign-in and ended at the app. A `baseUrl` ending in `//` or a `uiBasePath` starting with `//` would compose a path starting with `//`, which as a root-relative `Location` names another host. Config alone reaches that and no token rides that redirect, but the route treats it as no sign-in page: the `401`, one `warn`, and the server is not asked.

**`redirect` (constraint 4)** is rebuilt from the validated parameters only: `redirect_uri`, `code_challenge`, and `code_challenge_method` if the request had it. The app's `redirect_uri` stays nested inside `redirect`, because `redirect_uri` at the top of the page's query, with `client_id`, is what the page reads as an OAuth authorize replay.

**No Console (constraint 6).** The route asks the composed server, in-process and per request, for the sign-in page, and redirects only when that answers `200` with an HTML document. `readShellConfig` and `anonymousFormDoorServes` in `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` already ask the composed app the same way. A route table would not do: `os serve` mounts a `503` responder on the same paths when the Console was not built. So these all keep the `401`: `--no-ui`, a Console not built, a host that redirects `/_console` to the control plane. So does a Console served by something in front of this process, which is the cost of asking in-process: that deployment stays on today's JSON.

**The execution context.** `resolveHandoffSignInEntry` calls `server.fetch` with `env` and no execution context, and I left it that way because it cannot matter on any host read:

- `c.executionCtx` is read nowhere in this repo, nor in `objectstack-ai/cloud` at `f874972e`.
- In Hono itself only `middleware/cache` and `middleware/method-override` read it unguarded, and neither is imported here. `.mount()` reads it inside a `try`.
- No real request has one either. `plugin-hono-server` and cloud's `node-server.ts` serve through `@hono/node-server`, which calls `fetch(req, { incoming, outgoing })`, so the probe matches the request it came from. Cloud's Workers front a Node container and use `ctx.waitUntil` outside Hono. Cloud's Vercel entry calls `app.fetch(request)` alone.

`readShellConfig` already dispatches the same way, on every Console document. If a middleware ever did read it unguarded, the probe answers `500`, the route keeps the `401` and logs `it answers 500` once. A new pin holds that: it fails closed and says why.

**The loop (constraint 5) is real, and no longer happens.** Measured at `584f1e43fc`, in headless Chromium; the commit after it changes none of what these runs read. Every run below used a session really older than five minutes (each waited 5m10s). The device clock was set 15 minutes behind where the row says so.

| Run | Hand-off requests | Where it ended |
| --- | --- | --- |
| With Fetch Metadata, device clock behind, old session | 1: `302` (`none`) | The form, held for the 10 s watched; a sign-in on it ends in the `302` to the app |
| No Fetch Metadata, device clock behind, old session | 1: `302` | The form, held for the 10 s watched; a sign-in on it ends in the `302` to the app |
| With Fetch Metadata, session created after the mark, same URL reopened once stale | 1: `401` (`same-origin`) | JSON, and it stops |
| No Fetch Metadata, session created after the mark, same URL reopened once stale | 1: `302` | The form, under the newer mark, held for the 10 s watched |

For scale, the loop itself, measured earlier at `fe2b8b4907` with #29979 merged in, the same-origin stop removed and no page half: **228 hand-off requests in 20 s, all `302`**.

The session-created-after-the-mark rows are the remaining way the page forwards a session the route refuses: a URL reopened more than five minutes later. The same path covers a session the page can read and the route cannot, such as a bearer token with no cookie, which was read from the code and not run. "No Fetch Metadata" is Chromium behind a proxy that strips `sec-fetch-*`, so the server really sees none; no browser that truly lacks those headers was run.

**Why the mark is a time and not a bare mark.** `SocialSignInButtons` defaults `callbackURL` to `window.location.href`, so a provider sign-in comes back to the same URL with the mark still on it. A bare mark would then hold the form over the brand-new session, which is a dead end for exactly the Google users this flow exists for. With a time, the new session's `createdAt` is later and the page forwards. It also spares a device whose clock is ahead, where a fresh provider session read as too old. No identity provider exists on this machine, so that return was measured as a sign-in made elsewhere followed by opening the same URL again: it ended at the app with the device clock 15 minutes behind and 15 minutes ahead.

On one process the mark and `createdAt` are two readings of one clock. On several nodes behind one host they are two clocks, so skew can hold the form until a sign-in makes a later `createdAt`, which clears it. The docblocks say so.

**The mark across the sign-in pages.** `registerUrl` on `/login`, and on `/register` both `loginUrl` and the bounce a closed sign-up makes, now carry the mark beside a hand-off `redirect` (`handoffMarkQuery`). Beside any other `redirect`, or none, those links are byte-identical, and a test pins each.

Reading of `RegisterPage` with the mark, from the code and its pins. `useHandoffRedirect` reads the mark from the URL when it judges a session, so `/register` behaves as `/login` does. A session not created after the mark holds the form, whatever the device's clock says. A sign-up on that form changes the session to one with no `createdAt`, which is not the one found on arrival, so it forwards. A session created after the mark, which is a provider returning to this URL, forwards.

Measured at this PR's head, under the real router, with a route-issued mark, an old session and the device clock 15 minutes behind: `/login` held, "Sign up" to `/register` with the mark kept and the form held, "Sign in" back to `/login` with the mark kept and the form held, one hand-off request throughout; a sign-in then made the second hand-off request. The showcase is invite-only, so showing "Sign up" took patching the config response with Playwright interception, and under interception a `302` to the app's scheme reports `net::ERR_ABORTED`. A control with interception and no round trip reads the same. The `/register` to `/login` direction, run with no interception, read that second request as the `302`.

## Landing order and release

#29979 and #30004 are both on `main`, and the route and the page now change together in this PR, so nothing has to land first.

This carries in the next release after it merges: 18.4.0 as pending changesets stand (13 of 62 are `minor`, and these packages version together). objectstack-ai/mobile#190 can change its entry only once its server runs that release, because an older server answers the new entry with JSON.

## Tests

- `one-time-token-handoff.test.ts`: 88 tests on the real `AuthManager`, the real better-auth plugin and the real route registration. Page navigation with no session and with an old session gets the `302`; JSON, no headers, `*/*`, a `fetch` asking for HTML and an iframe get `401`; an unregistered scheme, a bad challenge, a plain method and an unknown parameter get `400` with no redirect; cross-site gets `400` first; the `redirect` it names signs in, comes back and redeems. A path starting with `//` gets the `401` and one `warn` and asks the server nothing. `resolveHandoffSignInEntry` and `isPageNavigation` have their own tables.
- `handoffRedirect-29971.test.ts` and `signInHandoff-29971.test.tsx` (the existing harness files for this component, so the new pins are top-level `describe`s there): a session created after `handoff_refused_at` is fresh and one not created after it is held, each with the device clock agreeing, an hour behind and an hour ahead; a value that is not digits is ignored and the five-minute check decides; a session with no `createdAt` keeps its branch; on the real `LoginPage` and `RegisterPage`, the form holds, a sign-in or sign-up on it forwards, and a session created after the mark forwards. Each of the three links carries the mark beside a hand-off `redirect` and stays byte-identical beside any other `redirect`, with no mark on the page, and with no `redirect`.
- Pins: the two existing `401` pins on the route send no navigation headers, so they stay and their titles now say so. No other pin of this route's `401` exists in the repo.
- `examples/app-showcase/e2e/mobile-signin-handoff.spec.ts`, two tests. Signed out, open the hand-off, land on the form on this origin, sign in, see the `302` to the registered scheme, and redeem the token with the verifier (and fail without it). And a sign-in made elsewhere that returns to the same URL forwards on a device whose clock is ahead, which is what notices the route and the page disagreeing on the parameter's name.

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the browser test lives, and that it is nightly.** Not `ui/e2e`: `Live E2E UI` serves the Console from `vite preview` at the root and the backend there has no built Console to serve, so the route's redirect has nothing to land on. `examples/app-showcase/e2e` is the one lane where the backend serves the Console at its real mount. It runs in Nightly Tiers and a red night files a card, so a Console change that breaks this shows up the next night, not on that PR. The two tests add about two seconds to that suite.
- **Scheme registration.** A test-only stack config works only at the app root (the compile resolves connector spec paths from the config's directory) and through `composeStacks` (a spread loses the `defineStack` provenance, and `defineStack` on a built stack reports 71 cross-reference issues), and every smoke spec would then boot a composed stack. `OS_TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES` on the `webServer` is one line and the path a deployment uses.
- **File surface beyond the first claim:** `examples/app-showcase/playwright.config.ts` (that one line), the doc comment of `examples/app-showcase/test/showcase-smoke.live.test.ts`, the page half, and `LoginPage.tsx` and `RegisterPage.tsx` only for the mark on the links between them, per the claim updates on the card.
- **One path still drops the mark.** `/verify-email-prompt` is given only `redirect` by both pages, and `VerifyEmailPromptPage`'s "back to login" builds `/login?redirect=…` from that. So a person sent there holding an old session, on a device whose clock is behind, who goes back is judged by the age check. A forward then ends at the route's `401` with Fetch Metadata, or at one more redirect whose mark holds the form without it. Read from the code, not run. It stops rather than loops. Left alone: `VerifyEmailPromptPage.tsx` is outside this card's surface.
- **Cloud does not offer this flow yet:** objectstack-ai/cloud#3549.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/principal-session-console-boot.dogfood.test.ts` skips on every CI run as far as the workflows read: none sets its Chromium path, and none builds the Console on that job. Noted, not filed.

**Declared narrowing — verification ran UNLOCKED.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` could not take the shared verify lock on this host: no usable `flock`. The shared verify lock is declared Linux-only (`flock` is util-linux, and a stock macOS does not ship it), so the commands above were run directly, without the lock — a declared narrowing, not a silent one. No serialization guarantee held for these runs, nor for any sibling agent in this container while they ran.
